title: Stolleis, European Twentieth-Century Dictatorship and the Law

1.title: How many farewells to the 19th century there were
1.text: We say the 19th century ended with the outbreak of war in August 1914 — and that divide really did have world-historical significance. But Stolleis at once adds: IN FACT THERE WERE SEVERAL FAREWELLS TO THE 19TH CENTURY AND EACH HAS A DIFFERENT DATE. In the decades before 1914 the remnants of the aristocratic and ecclesiastical ancien régime were displaced by a POLITICALLY AND ECONOMICALLY FAR STRONGER BOURGEOIS SOCIETY — which in turn feared the rise of the 'FOURTH ESTATE'. The INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION, begun already in the 18th century, now wholly dominated politics and society; in that connection the SOCIAL QUESTION and the international labour movement arose, SOCIAL INSURANCE came into being and ECONOMIC LIBERALISM GAVE WAY TO THE INTERVENTIONIST STATE. Parties and associations sprang up everywhere, the development towards modern parliamentarism set in — in short, the 'AGE OF THE MASSES' began. The fin-de-siècle atmosphere grew ever more hectic; the glamour and the darkness of the 'metropolis' fascinated but at the same time provoked a SENTIMENTAL LONGING TO ESCAPE THE CITIES FOR SIMPLE RURAL LIFE, and various rural communes, salvationist movements and sects arose SEEKING 'MEANING' AND LIBERATION FROM THE PRESSURES OF MODERNITY.

cards.q: Why does Stolleis say there were several farewells to the 19th century?
cards.a: Because the individual endings have different dates: in the decades before 1914 bourgeois society displaced the ancien régime; the industrial revolution dominated politics and society, the social question arose, social insurance came into being and economic liberalism gave way to the INTERVENTIONIST STATE; the 'age of the masses' began. August 1914 is only the most visible of those divides.

2.title: Fear after the war and why liberalism lost credibility
2.text: After the experience of a self-destroying European war — the new techniques of attritional warfare, MASS KILLING IN THE TRENCHES, THE USE OF POISON GAS, SUBMARINES — the 19th century seemed to lie in ruins. THE BALANCED 'LAISSEZ-FAIRE, LAISSEZ-ALLER' NO LONGER CONVINCED. LIBERALISM LOST CREDIBILITY. The structures that had made compromise between the bourgeoisie and constitutional monarchy possible were also threatened — the existing constitutional model, monarchy, parliamentarism — and the traditional concept of the state was weakened by the revolutions of 1917–1919. And yet: THE OLD NATION STATES HAD TO TAKE OVER CRISIS MANAGEMENT AFTER THE WAR, AND TO DO SO ON THE BASIS OF THE OLD PARTIES AND THE OLD PARLIAMENTARY AND CONSTITUTIONAL MODEL. The collapse of an apparently orderly world provoked FEAR, and Stolleis sets it out layer by layer: THE ARISTOCRACY lost its last privileges; THE BOURGEOISIE dreaded losing its central role and feared that Bolshevism would break out as in Russia; THE LOWER MIDDLE CLASS felt squeezed by communism on one side and big business on the other; the traditional values of family, home and nature seemed threatened; and SOLDIERS RETURNING FROM THE FRONT WERE UPROOTED AND LONGED FOR COMMUNITY, AUTHORITY AND LEADERSHIP, WHICH THEY FOUND EITHER IN RIGHT-WING OR IN LEFT-WING GROUPS. The 'ordinary' war was followed by civil wars and revolts, while Lenin proclaimed the imminence of world revolution. AND THE PARIS TREATIES WERE HUMILIATING FOR GERMANY, AUSTRIA AND HUNGARY: BY ASSIGNING GUILT THEY POISONED THE POST-WAR ATMOSPHERE. Italy did not get what the secret Treaty of London of 1915 had promised — and D'ANNUNZIO'S theatrical rule at FIUME and MUSSOLINI'S rise in MILAN brought into the world a SEMI-SOCIALIST, NATIONALIST-MILITARIST, AUTHORITARIAN FASCISM. After the MARCH ON ROME in October 1922 — which a year later inspired Hitler and Ludendorff in Munich — the Italian bourgeois state with its parliamentary democracy and rule of law was abolished.

cards.q: How does Stolleis set out post-war fear by social class?
cards.a: The aristocracy lost its last privileges; the bourgeoisie feared losing its central role and Bolshevism as in Russia; the lower middle class felt squeezed by communism and big business alike; and SOLDIERS RETURNING FROM THE FRONT WERE UPROOTED AND LONGED FOR COMMUNITY, AUTHORITY AND LEADERSHIP — which they found either in right-wing or in left-wing groups.

cards.q: What part do the Paris peace treaties play in the post-war atmosphere, on Stolleis's account?
cards.a: They were HUMILIATING for Germany, Austria and Hungary and BY ASSIGNING GUILT THEY POISONED THE POST-WAR ATMOSPHERE. To this, Italy did not get what the secret Treaty of London of 1915 had promised — hence D'Annunzio at Fiume and Mussolini's rise in Milan.

3.title: A map of the anti-liberal movements
3.text: All over Europe ANTI-LIBERAL AND AUTHORITARIAN MOVEMENTS gained political significance. SOME GREW OUT OF THE OLD CONSERVATIVE PARTIES which had criticised the constitutional monarchies from the right; OTHERS CAME OUT OF NEW SOCIAL-REVOLUTIONARY MOVEMENTS. In FRANCE the 'ACTION FRANÇAISE', led by the politicians Pujo, Gressent-Valois and Bucard, but also by intellectuals such as CHARLES MAURRAS and LÉON DAUDET. In SPAIN MIGUEL PRIMO DE RIVERA erected a dictatorship in 1923–1930, and from 1933 his son JOSÉ ANTONIO created the 'FALANGE ESPAÑOLA', from which after the civil war the rule of the 'CAUDILLO' FRANCISCO FRANCO emerged. In AUSTRIA the HEIMWEHREN arose, paramilitary groups aiming at a CHRISTIAN-SOCIAL CORPORATE STATE, which through contact with Italy took on fascist features. And the proof of contagion: EVEN IN ENGLAND, THE TRADITIONAL LAND OF PARLIAMENTARY DEMOCRACY, SIR OSWALD MOSLEY founded the 'BRITISH UNION OF FASCISTS' in 1932 — it remained insignificant, but its existence showed THAT FASCIST THINKING WAS HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS.

cards.q: What did the anti-liberal movements grow out of, and what does the British case prove?
cards.a: Some out of the OLD CONSERVATIVE PARTIES criticising the monarchies from the right, others out of NEW SOCIAL-REVOLUTIONARY movements. The British Union of Fascists founded by Sir Oswald Mosley in 1932 remained insignificant — but its existence in the traditional land of parliamentary democracy showed THAT FASCIST THINKING WAS HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS.

4.title: Parallels between right-wing and left-wing dictatorships
4.text: After the collapse of the Soviet Union and its satellites around 1989–1990 the historical view has clarified: IT IS NOW GENERALLY ACKNOWLEDGED THAT THE THEORIES OF TOTALITARIANISM DEVELOPED DURING THE COLD WAR WERE NOT WRONG IN POINTING TO CLEAR PARALLELS BETWEEN RIGHT-WING AND LEFT-WING DICTATORSHIPS. Both types of regime had in part COMMON INTELLECTUAL ORIGINS AND ANTIPATHIES; they relied on SIMILAR SYSTEMS OF STATE PROPAGANDA, SPIES AND SECRET STATE POLICE; both set up LABOUR AND EXTERMINATION CAMPS; and various CONTACTS AND TACIT AGREEMENTS between the systems are documented. And the most eloquent evidence: MANY BIOGRAPHIES SHOW THAT THE TRANSITION FROM LEFT-WING TO RIGHT-WING AUTHORITARIAN THINKING WAS OFTEN MUCH EASIER THAN THE TRANSITION FROM LIBERAL TO ANTI-LIBERAL. Overall: on one side the farewell to the 19th century brought THE END OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL MONARCHIES AND THE TRANSITION TO EGALITARIAN PARLIAMENTARY DEMOCRACIES; on the other the industrial revolution and the social movements created ENTIRELY NEW PROBLEMS AND ANXIETIES, AND WITH THEM NEW FORMS OF ANTI-DEMOCRATIC THINKING. Those ideologies fed longings for 'VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT', traditional ways of life, CHARISMATIC LEADERSHIP, 'UNITY' and the fight against the international features of the labour movement and of finance capital — driven by propaganda against MINORITIES, CORRUPTION, FOREIGN DOMINATION AND 'TRAITORS' of every kind. SUCH A VIEW OF THE WORLD AUTOMATICALLY MEANT A FIGHT AGAINST UNIVERSAL VALUES AND OBLIGATIONS, AGAINST THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS AND AGAINST THE RECONSTRUCTION OF EUROPE AFTER 1918.

cards.q: In what have the theories of totalitarianism been confirmed by the present view?
cards.a: In that there are clear parallels between right-wing and left-wing dictatorships: partly common intellectual origins and antipathies, similar systems of propaganda, spies and secret police, labour and extermination camps, documented mutual contacts — and many biographies show that THE TRANSITION FROM LEFT-WING TO RIGHT-WING AUTHORITARIAN THINKING WAS EASIER THAN THE TRANSITION FROM LIBERAL TO ANTI-LIBERAL.

cards.q: What did the anti-democratic ideologies promise, and what did they necessarily attack?
cards.a: They promised 'Volksgemeinschaft', traditional ways of life, charismatic leadership and 'unity', driven by propaganda against minorities, corruption, foreign domination and 'traitors'. Such a view of the world AUTOMATICALLY MEANT A FIGHT AGAINST UNIVERSAL VALUES AND OBLIGATIONS, AGAINST THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS AND THE RECONSTRUCTION OF EUROPE AFTER 1918.

5.title: What the right-wing regimes did with law
5.text: The individual right-wing regimes shaped their legal orders according to their ideological convictions. In order to reorganise labour according to the 'COMMON GOOD' they generally RESTRICTED FREEDOM OF CONTRACT AND FREEDOM OF ASSOCIATION IN FAVOUR OF THE OWNERS OF CAPITAL — reaching for CORPORATE, CORPORATIST OR SYNDICALIST models. Agrarian countries changed their LAND LAW. FAMILY LAW generally followed the ideal of the traditional family, UNLESS IT WAS REPLACED BY RACIST NOTIONS OF 'SELECTIVE BREEDING'. Direct discipline over people was exercised by the instruments of POLICE AND CRIMINAL LAW, which was tightened and supplemented with new offences. And here is the general formula best committed to memory: THE PUNISHMENT OF THE 'ACT', NARROWLY DEFINED IN A STATE UNDER THE RULE OF LAW, TENDED TO GIVE WAY TO THE PUNISHMENT OF THE 'PERPETRATOR', REGARDLESS OF THE PROHIBITION OF RETROACTIVITY (RÜCKWIRKUNGSVERBOT) AND THE PROHIBITION OF ANALOGY (ANALOGIEVERBOT). And in many cases the regimes created DARK ZONES OF LAWLESSNESS marked by arbitrary arrest, torture and execution.

terms.term: punishing the perpetrator instead of the act
terms.def: A general feature of the right-wing regimes: the narrowly defined 'act' gives way to punishing the 'perpetrator', breaking through the prohibitions of retroactivity and of analogy.

cards.q: What general shift in criminal law did the right-wing regimes bring?
cards.a: The punishment of the 'ACT', narrowly defined in a state under the rule of law, gave way to THE PUNISHMENT OF THE 'PERPETRATOR' — regardless of the PROHIBITION OF RETROACTIVITY and the PROHIBITION OF ANALOGY. To this were added dark zones of lawlessness with arbitrary arrest, torture and execution.

cards.q: What did the right-wing regimes do with labour and family law?
cards.a: To reorganise labour according to the 'common good' they RESTRICTED FREEDOM OF CONTRACT AND ASSOCIATION IN FAVOUR OF THE OWNERS OF CAPITAL, on corporatist or syndicalist models. Family law followed the ideal of the traditional family — UNLESS IT WAS REPLACED BY RACIST NOTIONS OF 'SELECTIVE BREEDING'.

6.title: Why Nazi law — and the only conclusion that can be drawn from it
6.text: The choice of Nazi Germany is doubly justified: by the WORLD-HISTORICAL IMPACT OF THE REGIME, which surpassed all other fascist systems in scale and destructive consequences — and by the fact that THE LEGAL ORDER OF 1933–1945 IS PARADIGMATIC. By analysing that well-researched order ONE CAN STUDY HOW REGIMES OPERATE IN THE TRANSITION FROM DEMOCRATIC-CONSTITUTIONAL TO AUTHORITARIAN AND FINALLY TO TOTALITARIAN FORMS — and especially HOW THE LIBERAL AND DEMOCRATIC ELITES OF ADMINISTRATION AND JUDICIARY COME TO TERMS WITH A NEW REGIME. Stolleis at the same time warns methodologically against the maxim 'HISTORIA DOCET', because NORMATIVE CONSEQUENCES CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM FACTUAL FINDINGS. And yet one conclusion can be drawn from that panorama, and it is the most important sentence of the whole article: ANTI-DEMOCRATIC 'MOVEMENTS' OR GOVERNMENTS THAT ATTACK THE UNIVERSALITY OF HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS, THAT OBSTRUCT FREE COMMUNICATION AND REPLACE IT WITH PROPAGANDA, THAT SEIZE THE JUDICIARY AND SEEK TO CRIMINALISE THEIR POLITICAL OPPONENTS, MUST BE RECOGNISED AND POLITICALLY OPPOSED AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE — on the assumption, of course, that we regard democracy, human rights, civil rights and the rule of law as worth defending.

cards.q: Why is the Nazi legal order paradigmatic?
cards.a: Because it allows one to study HOW REGIMES OPERATE IN THE TRANSITION FROM DEMOCRATIC-CONSTITUTIONAL TO AUTHORITARIAN AND FINALLY TO TOTALITARIAN FORMS — and especially HOW THE LIBERAL AND DEMOCRATIC ELITES OF ADMINISTRATION AND JUDICIARY COME TO TERMS WITH A NEW REGIME. It is also the best researched.

cards.q: What single conclusion does Stolleis draw from the history of the dictatorships — and with what reservation?
cards.a: That anti-democratic movements or governments which ATTACK THE UNIVERSALITY OF HUMAN RIGHTS, OBSTRUCT FREE COMMUNICATION AND REPLACE IT WITH PROPAGANDA, SEIZE THE JUDICIARY AND CRIMINALISE OPPONENTS must be recognised and opposed as early as possible. The reservation: normative consequences cannot be derived from factual findings ('historia docet' does not hold), so the conclusion holds only for those who regard democracy and the rule of law as worth defending.

7.title: Three senses of 'Nazi law'
7.text: One can speak of Nazi law IN THREE SENSES. NARROWLY defined it means ALL IDEOLOGICALLY SHAPED LAWS — the race laws, hereditary farm law, marriage law, deprivation of citizenship. MORE BROADLY it means ALL STATUTE LAW AND CASE LAW NEWLY CREATED BETWEEN 1933 AND 1945. AND IN THE BROADEST SENSE THE WHOLE LEGAL ORDER THAT WAS APPLIED, PRACTISED AND TAUGHT (COMMUNICATED) UNDER NAZISM. The distinction was not merely academic: it mattered for the Allied regulations on the 'LIBERATION OF THE GERMAN PEOPLE FROM NAZISM AND MILITARISM', for denazification, and for the problem that STATUTES AND STATE TREATIES REMAINED IN FORCE UNTIL THE BUNDESTAG FIRST MET (art. 123 of the Basic Law). It mattered for the courts too — both because of the continuing validity of norms and legal relations from that period and because of judicial decisions WHICH COULD NOT BE DECLARED VOID A PRIORI. And it reflects THE STAGES OF THE GRADUAL EXAMINATION OF THE NAZI PAST: at first scholars concentrated on injustice and suffering and on norms contrary to the 'FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF JUSTICE'; then the field widened to legislative, administrative and judicial practice and to Nazi legal scholarship itself — which was necessary IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND THE COMMUNICATION NETWORK OF ALL THE ACTORS IN THE SYSTEM.

cards.q: Name the three senses of the term 'Nazi law' and say why the distinction mattered.
cards.a: 1) Narrowly: ideologically shaped laws (race laws, hereditary farm law, marriage law, deprivation of citizenship). 2) More broadly: all statute and case law newly created between 1933 and 1945. 3) Most broadly: the whole legal order applied, practised and taught under Nazism. It mattered for denazification, for the continuing validity of norms and treaties until the Bundestag first met (art. 123 GG), and for decisions that could not be declared void a priori.

8.title: Two periods of reckoning and the legend of positivism
8.text: THE FIRST PERIOD was dominated by eyewitness accounts, horror, perplexity and a profession of faith in democracy and natural law; the questions 'how could it happen?', 'whose fault was it?' and 'what now?' were asked LESS FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF KNOWLEDGE THAN AS PART OF A POLITICAL PROGRAMME. Typical was a RENAISSANCE OF NATURAL LAW and of value philosophy — and just as after 1933, GENERAL CLAUSES and vague legal concepts were seen as THE POINTS THROUGH WHICH VALUES ENTER THE SYSTEM, now of course the values of a democratic constitution. To this period belong the NUREMBERG TRIALS and thousands of German proceedings over Nazi violence; IT ENDED AROUND 1952 — in the West halted by the Cold War and the 'economic miracle', in the East by a self-definition as fundamentally 'ANTI-FASCIST'. Open and concealed amnesties for lesser offenders went hand in hand with A GENERAL STRATEGY OF EXCULPATING THE ENTIRE PERSONNEL OF JUDICIARY AND ADMINISTRATION; the same applied to legal scholars, who either denied or played down their writings after 1933. And here is the legend that must be named: IT WAS GENERALLY BELIEVED THAT LAWYERS HAD ULTIMATELY BEEN VICTIMS OF A SYSTEM CONTEMPTUOUS OF LAW, AND THAT THEIR CONDUCT WAS DUE TO THE LEGAL-POSITIVIST APPROACH THEY HAD ABSORBED IN THEIR STUDIES — because public injustice through statute was supposedly hard to imagine. THE SECOND PERIOD was opened by the ULM EINSATZKOMMANDO TRIAL and the founding of the CENTRAL OFFICE FOR THE INVESTIGATION OF NAZI CRIMES AT LUDWIGSBURG IN 1958; in 1960 EICHMANN was tried in Israel and in 1963–1965 the AUSCHWITZ TRIAL was held in Frankfurt at the instance of the attorney general FRITZ BAUER.

cards.q: What legend arose in the first period of reckoning with the Nazi past?
cards.a: That LAWYERS HAD ULTIMATELY BEEN VICTIMS of a system contemptuous of law and that their conduct was due to the LEGAL-POSITIVIST APPROACH absorbed in their studies, because public injustice through statute was supposedly hard to imagine. It went hand in hand with amnesties for lesser offenders and a general strategy of exculpating the whole personnel of judiciary and administration.

cards.q: What ended the first and what began the second period of reckoning?
cards.a: The first ended around 1952 — in the West with the Cold War and the 'economic miracle', in the East with a self-definition as fundamentally 'anti-fascist'. The second was opened by the Ulm Einsatzkommando trial and the founding of the CENTRAL OFFICE AT LUDWIGSBURG IN 1958, then the Eichmann trial in Israel (1960) and the Auschwitz trial in Frankfurt (1963–65) at Fritz Bauer's instance.

9.title: The paradox: a criminal regime makes law
9.text: Hitler HAD NO RESPECT FOR LAW and did not think highly of lawyers, especially when they raised objections — BUT HE SAW THEM AS USEFUL INSTRUMENTS: already in the early years he used criminal proceedings as a political weapon, and later lawyers helped him dismantle the Weimar constitution and formulate legislative projects. In his last years he often spoke of lawyers disparagingly, as preserved in the 'table talk' — and AFTER 1945 LAWYERS POINTED TO THOSE REMARKS TO SUPPORT THE MYTH THAT THEY HAD BEEN LAW-ABIDING OPPONENTS OF THE TYRANT AND HIS 'VICTIMS'. That view has now been corrected. And now the legal paradox. Hitler at once used emergency decree powers to ABOLISH THE FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS that stood in his way, and when shortly afterwards he stripped parliament of power, NO DEMOCRATICALLY CONTROLLED PROCESS OF LAW-MAKING REMAINED. BUT FORMALLY SPEAKING LAW WENT ON BEING MADE — AND THAT LAW WAS USABLE, ALTHOUGH ITS CONSTITUTIONAL BASIS NO LONGER EXISTED. To claim that all legal acts of 1933–1945 were void IS POSSIBLE ONLY IN THEORY; in practice it cannot be maintained, because COUNTLESS LEGAL ACTS REMAINED IN FORCE, especially in civil, commercial and administrative law, but in international law too. ONE MUST ACCEPT THE PARADOX THAT A CRIMINAL REGIME CAN MAKE LAW, and examine case by case which elements of Nazi law were legally valid and which must be regarded as acts standing a priori outside the legal order, and therefore void from the outset. And between those two extremes lie TWO FURTHER CATEGORIES: NORMS LEGALLY VALID BUT MORALLY OUTRAGEOUS — and ACTS MORALLY PERMISSIBLE BUT UNLAWFUL, SUCH AS ARMED RESISTANCE TO THE REGIME.

cards.q: What paradox must be accepted about Nazi law, on Stolleis's account, and what four categories follow from it?
cards.a: The paradox that A CRIMINAL REGIME CAN MAKE LAW — claiming that all acts of 1933–45 were void is possible only in theory, because countless ones remained in force. Four categories: legally valid acts; acts standing a priori outside the legal order and therefore void from the outset; NORMS LEGALLY VALID BUT MORALLY OUTRAGEOUS; and ACTS MORALLY PERMISSIBLE BUT UNLAWFUL, such as armed resistance to the regime.

cards.q: How did Hitler treat lawyers and how did they use that after the war?
cards.a: He had no respect for law and did not think highly of lawyers, but SAW THEM AS USEFUL INSTRUMENTS — he used criminal proceedings as a political weapon and had them dismantle the Weimar constitution. After 1945 lawyers pointed to his disparaging remarks in the 'table talk' to support THE MYTH THAT THEY HAD BEEN LAW-ABIDING OPPONENTS OF THE TYRANT AND HIS 'VICTIMS'.

10.title: The dismantling of the constitutional state step by step
10.text: By emergency decree under ARTICLE 48 OF THE WEIMAR CONSTITUTION the FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS WERE IMMEDIATELY SUSPENDED (the REICHSTAGSBRANDVERORDNUNG, 28 FEBRUARY 1933). A wave of unlawful measures followed: the first CAMPS for detaining opponents, justified to the public by the deceptive term 'PROTECTIVE CUSTODY'; the first violence against German Jews; and the term 'JEWISH' openly acquired a RACIAL meaning in the legal sphere. Political parties were banned and the NSDAP acquired the rank of universal state party. Parliamentary democracy ended with the ENABLING ACT (24 MARCH 1933), renewed twice, until Hitler on 30 JANUARY 1939 extended it INDEFINITELY by decree. The new leadership took over the bureaucracy and purged it of political opponents and Jews; the GLEICHSCHALTUNG OF THE LÄNDER destroyed the federal order, so that the REICHSRAT became superfluous. After the death of President HINDENBURG in 1934 HIS OFFICE too was abolished. THERE REMAINED ONLY THE 'FÜHRER' AND THE GREETING 'HEIL HITLER!', whose use became compulsory in all official and private intercourse. A CONSTITUTION IN THE USUAL SENSE NO LONGER EXISTED; the literature did try to assemble a kind of constitution out of the most important Nazi statutes, BUT THAT NORMATIVE FRAMEWORK WAS NEVER MEANT TO BIND THE EXERCISE OF STATE POWER BY LAW.

cards.q: Name the steps by which the Weimar constitutional state was dismantled.
cards.a: The emergency decree under art. 48 suspended fundamental rights (28 Feb 1933); the first camps under the pretext of 'protective custody'; the banning of parties and the NSDAP as universal state party; the ENABLING ACT (24 March 1933), extended indefinitely in 1939; the purge of the bureaucracy; the GLEICHSCHALTUNG OF THE LÄNDER, which destroyed federalism and made the Reichsrat superfluous; and after Hindenburg's death in 1934 the abolition of the office of president.

11.title: The dual state and its transformation into an SS state
11.text: Uncertainty about the 'FÜHRER'S WILL', to which appeal was repeatedly made, endowed the party apparatus with enormous power BUT UNDERMINED THE LEGAL STRUCTURES OF THE STATE FROM WITHIN. Alongside statutes there existed 'MEASURES' AND 'FÜHRER ORDERS', many of which were no longer published. TWO WORLDS EXISTED SIDE BY SIDE: THE ORDERLY APPLICATION OF LAW AND OPEN TERROR (Ernst Fraenkel, DOPPELSTAAT). And here is the sentence that matters most: THE ZONES OF THE FORMER WERE MAINTAINED NOT LEAST IN ORDER TO SILENCE THE CONSCIENCES OF BUREAUCRATS AND JUDGES, WHOSE COOPERATION WAS STILL REGARDED AS INDISPENSABLE — BUT THOSE AREAS OF 'NORMALITY' WERE UNDERMINED BY THE FACT THAT THEY COULD BE DEMOLISHED AT ANY MOMENT BY AN APPEAL TO THE 'COMMON GOOD'. The dual state gradually turned into an 'SS STATE'. And Stolleis's probable conjecture: FOR LACK OF REGULARITY THE SYSTEM WOULD HAVE LOST ITS CAPACITY FOR SELF-ORGANISATION EVEN WITHOUT THE WAR, and sooner or later would have collapsed. After 1933 everything built up in the legal system since the 19th century was dismantled — partly by statute, partly by political pressure. Trade unions, professional chambers and associations of every kind were abolished or absorbed; RESISTANCE COULD BE OFFERED ONLY BY THE CHURCHES IN THE 'KIRCHENKAMPF', but they thereby largely lost control of their social institutions. As early as 11 MARCH 1933 GOEBBELS'S MINISTRY OF POPULAR ENLIGHTENMENT AND PROPAGANDA was created and THE PRESS LOST ITS INDEPENDENCE WITHIN SIX MONTHS. The result was a MILITARISED, AUTHORITARIAN UNITARY STATE which tried to reconcile conflicting interests by preaching a new 'IDEOLOGY' — AND MADE IT BINDING FOR THE INTERPRETATION OF ALL LEGAL NORMS. Officially administrative jurisdiction remained and THE JUDGES REMAINED INDEPENDENT UNTIL 1942, but in practice these pillars of the rule of law were gradually undermined until they became insignificant.

terms.def: Fraenkel's concept: the orderly application of law and open terror exist side by side. The zones of 'normality' are maintained to silence the consciences of officials — and can be demolished at any moment by appeal to the 'common good'.

cards.q: What is the 'dual state' and why did the regime maintain zones of normality at all?
cards.a: THE ORDERLY APPLICATION OF LAW AND OPEN TERROR existed side by side. The zones of normality were maintained TO SILENCE THE CONSCIENCES OF BUREAUCRATS AND JUDGES whose cooperation was indispensable — but they were undermined by the fact that they COULD BE DEMOLISHED AT ANY MOMENT BY AN APPEAL TO THE 'COMMON GOOD'. The dual state gradually turned into an 'SS state'.

cards.q: Were judges independent under Nazism?
cards.a: Formally YES, UNTIL 1942, and administrative jurisdiction officially remained — but in practice these pillars of the rule of law were gradually undermined until they became insignificant. The new 'ideology' was moreover made BINDING FOR THE INTERPRETATION OF ALL LEGAL NORMS.

12.title: Deprivation of rights: and it happened within the law
12.text: Opponents of the regime lost their citizenship, and the discrimination and persecution of Jews and of political, religious and ethnic minorities began. It all started with a series of CUNNING AND PERFIDIOUS DEPRIVATIONS OF RIGHTS under the pretext of 'ARYANISATION': confiscation of property and expropriation, the seizure of businesses, THE THEFT OF ART, the order that all Jews use the names 'ISRAEL' AND 'SARA', the introduction of the Jewish star. These measures reached a new level with THE POGROMS GOEBBELS UNLEASHED BETWEEN 9 AND 11 NOVEMBER 1938. The culmination was the murder of millions in the extermination camps, extended to all European Jews after the war of conquest began. And now the sentence most important to remember: WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE ABOMINABLE FINAL PHASE, THE DISCRIMINATION AGAINST AND DEPRIVATION OF RIGHTS OF JEWS AND OTHERS TOOK PLACE WITHIN THE LAW — THE MEASURES IN QUESTION WERE PUBLISHED AND LAWYERS COMMENTED ON THEM. The individual attempts to explain this — antisemitism, a traditional spirit of subservience and the influence of various 'milieux', envy and personal enrichment, propaganda, the unleashing of an always latent aggression against minorities — illuminate, on Stolleis's view, ONLY PARTS OF THE PROBLEM. And it is remarkable that in explaining the obedience of lawyers historians have pointed BOTH TO LEGAL POSITIVISM AND TO THE MARKED ANTI-POSITIVISM THE REGIME CULTIVATED IN ITS CONTEMPT FOR LAW — that is, to two contrary things at once.

cards.q: Did the deprivation of Jews' rights take place outside the law or within it?
cards.a: WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE ABOMINABLE FINAL PHASE IT TOOK PLACE WITHIN THE LAW: the measures were PUBLISHED AND LAWYERS COMMENTED ON THEM. It was a series of 'Aryanisations' — confiscation, expropriation, the seizure of businesses, the theft of art, the order to use the names 'Israel' and 'Sara', the Jewish star — culminating in the pogroms of 9–11 November 1938.

13.title: Judges: why the legend of positivism does not hold
13.text: The Nazis began in most traditional fields WITHOUT CONCEPTS AND WITHOUT EXPERTS — the one exception being agricultural policy, with older models of a corporate structure under state direction, quickly realised as the 'REICHSNÄHRSTAND' and supplemented by 'BLOOD AND SOIL' legislation which revived many ARCHAIC LEGAL CONCEPTS. The first concern was TO RESTAFF THE ADMINISTRATION AND THE JUDICIARY; the judiciary was purged of ideological opponents and the remaining judges were brought under control by TRAINING PROGRAMMES, 'COMMUNITY CAMPS', INDOCTRINATION THROUGH THE PRESS AND THE PREACHING OF PRINCIPLES. HANS FRANK, the Reichsjuristenführer, proclaimed semi-officially: 'THE BASIS FOR THE INTERPRETATION OF ALL LEGAL SOURCES IS THE NATIONAL SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY, AS EXPRESSED PARTICULARLY IN THE PARTY PROGRAMME AND IN THE UTTERANCES OF OUR FÜHRER. JUDGES HAVE NO RIGHT TO REVIEW DECISIONS OF THE FÜHRER ISSUED IN THE FORM OF STATUTES OR LEGAL ORDINANCES. JUDGES ARE ALSO BOUND BY ALL OTHER DECISIONS OF THE FÜHRER, PROVIDED IT IS BEYOND DOUBT THAT THEY ARE INTENDED TO CREATE LAW.' And Stolleis's key argument: AT THE BEGINNING AND AT THE END OF THE REGIME, IDEOLOGICALLY MOTIVATED INTERPRETATION OF OLD LAW WAS MUCH SIMPLER AND MORE EFFECTIVE THAN PASSING NEW STATUTES THROUGH A SLOW LEGISLATIVE PROCESS. The instrumentalisation of the legal order therefore proceeded ALONG TWO PATHS: alongside Führer edicts and hasty legislation it was ABOVE ALL THE POLITICISED ALIGNMENT OF THE JUDICIARY that changed the established law — and in many branches the IDEOLOGICAL OVERPAINTING OF THE OLD BODY OF NORMS WAS MORE IMPORTANT THAN LEGISLATION. It is therefore only partly true that judges were at the mercy of unrestrained legislators because of their positivism; as a summary description of judicial decision-making that thesis, widespread in the 1950s, is SIMPLY MISLEADING. ALREADY UNDER THE WEIMAR REPUBLIC MANY JUDGES HAD TURNED AGAINST THE DEMOCRATICALLY LEGITIMATED LEGISLATOR — they therefore had no methodological difficulty in overcoming 'narrow normativism', as the regime demanded, by interpreting according to 'CONCRETE IDEAS OF ORDER AND SHAPING', 'THE WILL OF THE FÜHRER', 'THE NEEDS OF THE VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT', 'THE COMMON GOOD', 'GOOD FAITH', 'BREACH OF GOOD MORALS' OR 'THE HEALTHY SENTIMENT OF THE PEOPLE'.

cards.q: Why does Stolleis reject the thesis that judges were at the mercy of legislators because of their positivism?
cards.a: Because ALREADY UNDER THE WEIMAR REPUBLIC MANY JUDGES HAD TURNED AGAINST THE DEMOCRATICALLY LEGITIMATED LEGISLATOR, and they therefore had no difficulty overcoming 'narrow normativism' by interpreting according to 'the will of the Führer', 'the needs of the Volksgemeinschaft', 'the common good', 'good faith' or 'the healthy sentiment of the people'. As a summary description of judicial decision-making, that 1950s thesis is MISLEADING.

cards.q: What was more effective than new legislation, and why?
cards.a: IDEOLOGICALLY MOTIVATED INTERPRETATION OF OLD LAW — at the beginning and at the end of the regime it was much simpler and more effective than passing new statutes through a slow legislative process. The instrumentalisation of law therefore ran along two paths: Führer edicts and hasty legislation, but ABOVE ALL THE POLITICISED ALIGNMENT OF THE JUDICIARY.

cards.q: Quote Frank's directive on the interpretation of law.
cards.a: 'The basis for the interpretation of all legal sources is the National Socialist ideology, as expressed particularly in the party programme and in the utterances of our Führer. Judges have no right to review decisions of the Führer issued in the form of statutes or legal ordinances. Judges are also bound by all other decisions of the Führer, provided it is beyond doubt that they are intended to create law.'

14.title: Administrative law: five inversions
14.text: The Gleichschaltung of the Länder turned every branch of administration into a part of Reich administration, and the limited autonomy of the municipalities was abolished too. BUT THIS DID NOT PRODUCE A MONOLITHIC UNITARY STATE: the federal structures were replaced by UNPREDICTABLE RIVALRIES AMONG GAULEITERS AND CONSTANT FRICTION BETWEEN STATE AND PARTY. General administrative law, shaped by the rule of law, was undermined after 1933 in theory and in practice — and Stolleis lists FIVE INVERSIONS the Nazis demanded: 1) TO SUSPEND THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN STATUTE, LEGAL ORDINANCE AND INDIVIDUAL ACT which the constitutional state had developed; 2) TO INVERT THE FUNCTION OF NORMS FROM A LIMIT ON ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION INTO ITS GOAL; 3) TO REPLACE 'LEGALITY' (GESETZMÄSSIGKEIT) WITH AN IDEOLOGICALLY DETERMINED 'RIGHTNESS' (RECHTMÄSSIGKEIT); 4) TO DISPLACE A LEGAL STATUS FOUNDED ON RIGHTS BY ONE FOUNDED ON DUTIES; and 5) TO REPLACE THE TERM 'ADMINISTRATIVE LAW' IN COMMON USAGE BY THE TERM 'ADMINISTRATION', in the titles of university lectures for instance. In addition the Nazis successfully restricted judicial review of broadly defined 'EXTRA-LEGAL SOVEREIGN ACTS', above all BY EXEMPTING THE POLITICAL POLICE FROM COMPLIANCE WITH LEGAL RULES, and suppressed private legal positions by reference to 'PUBLIC NECESSITIES' in construction, armaments and warfare. ADMINISTRATIVE JURISDICTION on the one hand survived and even seemed to gain influence when a Führer edict of 3 April 1941 established a REICH ADMINISTRATIVE COURT — on the other hand conservative and radical forces fought over that institution and it GRADUALLY DECLINED INTO INSIGNIFICANCE. The number of actions fell sharply, BECAUSE TO TELL THE NAZI STATE THAT IT HAD ACTED UNLAWFULLY WAS NOT WITHOUT DANGER.

cards.q: List the demands by which the Nazis inverted administrative law.
cards.a: To suspend the distinction between statute, ordinance and individual act; TO INVERT THE FUNCTION OF NORMS FROM A LIMIT ON ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION INTO ITS GOAL; to replace 'legality' with an ideologically determined 'rightness'; to displace a status founded on RIGHTS by one founded on DUTIES; and to replace the term 'administrative law' with 'administration'. Plus the exemption of the political police from legal rules.

cards.q: Did the Gleichschaltung produce a monolithic unitary state?
cards.a: NO. The federal structures were replaced by UNPREDICTABLE RIVALRIES AMONG GAULEITERS AND CONSTANT FRICTION BETWEEN STATE AND PARTY. The federal character moreover persisted in the personnel and structures of the Land administrations and in the special administrative law of the individual Länder.

15.title: Civil law: the general clauses as a gateway
15.text: Civil law largely retained its core of norms, BUT EXPERIENCED A CONSIDERABLE SHIFT OF EMPHASIS, especially through changes in case law and doctrine. And here is the irony worth being able to state: SHORTLY BEFORE 1933 LAWYERS WERE STILL WARNING AGAINST THE GENERAL CLAUSES OF THE BGB (§§ 138, 157, 162, 226, 242, 826) — NOW THE SAME PARAGRAPHS WERE PRAISED AS PROVISIONS THAT ALLOW NAZI IDEOLOGY TO ENTER CIVIL LAW. This matched the general strategy of giving law a political orientation BY STRENGTHENING ITS DETERRENT FUNCTION WHILE WEAKENING ITS CAPACITY TO MAINTAIN ORDER. The proclaimed break-up of the BGB into individual statutes was never carried out, any more than the creation of a 'VOLKSGESETZBUCH' which was to adapt the BGB and the Austrian ABGB to Nazi ideology. Outside the core of the BGB, however, much changed: the legislator intervened in MARRIAGE, FAMILY AND 'HEREDITARY HEALTH' LAW, and in the regulation of adoption, the contesting of paternity, MARRIAGE LOANS, maintenance, COMPULSORY STERILISATION and a new divorce law, DEMOGRAPHIC, EUGENIC AND RACIST MOTIVES MERGED. Exclusively antisemitic was the so-called BLOOD PROTECTION LAW OF 15 SEPTEMBER 1935 — and lawyers later often claimed that they had interpreted the whole range of deranged provisions 'WITH THE INTENTION OF MITIGATING THEM'.

cards.q: What became of the general clauses of the BGB after 1933?
cards.a: An ironic reversal: shortly before 1933 lawyers were still WARNING against them, and now the same paragraphs (§§ 138, 157, 162, 226, 242, 826) were PRAISED AS PROVISIONS THAT ALLOW NAZI IDEOLOGY TO ENTER CIVIL LAW. It matched the strategy of STRENGTHENING THE DETERRENT FUNCTION OF LAW AND WEAKENING ITS CAPACITY TO MAINTAIN ORDER.

cards.q: Which of the announced civil law reforms were never carried out?
cards.a: The proclaimed BREAK-UP OF THE BGB into individual statutes, and equally the creation of a 'VOLKSGESETZBUCH' to adapt the BGB and the Austrian ABGB to Nazi ideology. Civil law therefore kept the core of the BGB's norms — what changed chiefly was marriage, family and 'hereditary health' law.

16.title: Labour and social law: carrot and stick
16.text: The separation of labour law from the BGB led to A COMPLETE BREAK WITH TRADITION, because a FASCIST-CORPORATIST MODEL was adopted: THE TRADE UNIONS WERE SMASHED AND COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AUTONOMY ABOLISHED. The relation of employer and employee mutated into an ETHICISED COMMUNITY meant to benefit people and state while preserving the economic basis; the GERMAN LABOUR FRONT was to unite both sides, BUT IN PRACTICE STRONGLY FAVOURED EMPLOYERS — by banning strikes, controlling wages and restricting the free choice of workplace. At the same time, however: UNEMPLOYMENT WAS ELIMINATED BY PUBLIC WORKS AND REARMAMENT, propaganda placed the labour of 'BROW AND FIST' (STIRN UND FAUST) on an equal footing, the leisure programme 'STRENGTH THROUGH JOY' (KRAFT DURCH FREUDE) was created and a range of further measures to satisfy employees was adopted. COMBINED WITH THE STRICT CONTROL OF THE SPECIAL COURTS AND THE GESTAPO, THIS ENABLED THE REGIME TO PREVENT UNREST AND SABOTAGE LARGELY THROUGHOUT THE WAR. Similarly in social law: in public welfare, church and independent activities were suppressed and replaced by the 'WINTER RELIEF OF THE GERMAN PEOPLE'. As early as 1935 the German Labour Front complained that funds were being spent on 'HOPELESSLY SICK AND UNDOUBTEDLY INFERIOR PERSONS' to an 'EXCESSIVE DEGREE' — the aim being not only to promote eugenics but TO ENCOURAGE THE KILLING OF 'USELESS EATERS'. The regime DARED TO BEGIN SYSTEMATIC KILLING ('EUTHANASIA') ONLY AFTER THE WAR BROKE OUT AND HAD TO STOP IT WHEN THE CHURCHES SPOKE OUT AGAINST IT. In social insurance the number of insurance funds fell by more than 2,800 to a little over 4,800 by 1939, benefits improved and the circle of entitled persons widened; BUT THE FULL PICTURE INCLUDES the destruction of the funds' self-government in favour of the leadership principle, the fact that JEWS AND OPPONENTS OF THE REGIME HAD THEIR BENEFITS CUT OR ABOLISHED ENTIRELY, that temporarily raised contributions became permanent, and that THE ASSETS OF SOCIAL INSURANCE WERE USED TO FINANCE THE WAR. The regime's aim was TO KEEP A FUNCTIONING SYSTEM SO AS TO USE IT FOR WAR PURPOSES, to avoid antagonising broad sections of the population and, by improving benefits, TO STABILISE THE 'HOME FRONT'.

cards.q: How did the Nazi regime combine the smashing of the trade unions with social peace?
cards.a: It smashed the unions and abolished bargaining autonomy; the German Labour Front strongly favoured employers by banning strikes, controlling wages and restricting the choice of workplace. But it also eliminated unemployment by public works and rearmament, put the labour of 'brow and fist' on an equal footing and created 'Strength through Joy'. COMBINED WITH THE CONTROL OF THE SPECIAL COURTS AND THE GESTAPO THIS LARGELY PREVENTED UNREST AND SABOTAGE THROUGHOUT THE WAR.

cards.q: Why did the Nazis improve social insurance, and what completes that picture?
cards.a: To keep a functioning system, USE IT FOR WAR PURPOSES, avoid antagonising broad sections of the population and stabilise the 'home front'. It must be completed by the destruction of the funds' self-government in favour of the leadership principle, the CUTTING OR ABOLITION OF BENEFITS FOR JEWS AND OPPONENTS, the permanence of raised contributions, and THE USE OF THE INSURANCE ASSETS TO FINANCE THE WAR.

cards.q: When did the regime dare to begin 'euthanasia' and what stopped it?
cards.a: ONLY AFTER THE WAR BROKE OUT — and it had to stop WHEN THE CHURCHES SPOKE OUT AGAINST IT. It had been prepared by the German Labour Front's complaint of 1935 that 'excessively much' was being spent on 'hopelessly sick and undoubtedly inferior persons'.

17.title: Tax law as a specimen of the whole mechanism
17.text: Stolleis's most elegant illustration: THE TENSION BETWEEN THE APPARENTLY APOLITICAL TECHNICALITY OF A BRANCH OF LAW AND ITS DOMINATION BY A GENERAL CLAUSE PLACED ABOVE IT. § 1 OF THE TAX ADAPTATION ACT (STEUERANPASSUNGSGESETZ) OF 16 OCTOBER 1934 provided that TAX LAW WAS TO BE INTERPRETED ACCORDING TO 'NATIONAL SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY' — and that provision was soon understood AS THE LEADING PRINCIPLE OF INTERPRETATION FOR ALL BRANCHES OF LAW. It had a markedly adverse effect on the organisations the Nazis despised — Jewish associations of every kind, hospitals, old people's homes, church foundations, religious orders and other ideologically oriented institutions — BECAUSE MOST OF THEM LOST THEIR CHARITABLE STATUS. At the same time the payment of tax was proclaimed AN ACT OF LOYALTY and tax evasion condemned as 'TREASON AGAINST THE VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT'. And the point: DESPITE THE LEGEND OF THE PURELY TECHNICAL ORIENTATION OF THE FISCAL COURTS, THE CASE LAW OF THE REICH FISCAL COURT FAVOURED THE REGIME by contributing significantly to the tightening of taxable events and actively worsening the position of — above all — Jewish associations and the churches.

cards.q: Why is tax law a good specimen of the whole Nazi mechanism?
cards.a: Because it shows the tension between the apparently apolitical technicality of a branch and its domination by A GENERAL CLAUSE PLACED ABOVE IT: § 1 of the Tax Adaptation Act of 16 October 1934 ordered tax law to be interpreted according to 'National Socialist ideology' — and that soon became the leading principle of interpretation FOR ALL BRANCHES. Jewish associations, hospitals, church foundations and orders thereby lost their charitable status.

18.title: Criminal law: what the regime needed it for
18.text: From the outset the Nazis understood and exploited THE POLITICAL FUNCTION OF CRIMINAL LAW: TO INTIMIDATE POLITICAL OPPONENTS, SUPPRESS MINORITIES, CREATE FEAR — NOT LEAST AMONG THEIR OWN FOLLOWERS — AND TO WELD THE VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT TOGETHER BY CRIMINALISING A FEW EXPOSED VICTIMS, such as the so-called 'NOVEMBER CRIMINALS', communists and Jews. To this they promised to restore public order and, under point 18 of the NSDAP programme, to wage a 'RUTHLESS FIGHT AGAINST THOSE WHOSE ACTIVITY HARMS THE COMMON GOOD'. There was NO PROGRAMME of criminal law reform in 1933, but there was an ANTI-LIBERAL, ANTI-RATIONAL AND ANTI-INDIVIDUALIST TONE shared by a considerable part of the specialist literature. Out of these premises grew a system of criminal control and repression, beginning with raids under the REICHSTAG FIRE DECREE OF 28 FEBRUARY 1933. As important as the tightening was that THE REGIME ABOLISHED THE PROHIBITION OF RETROACTIVITY AND THE PROHIBITION OF ANALOGY and introduced the possibility of founding criminal liability where it was clear that the accused had committed a crime but not which of several (WAHLFESTSTELLUNG) — thereby violating the principle IN DUBIO PRO REO. THESE MEASURES UNDERMINED THE VERY CORE OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE UNDER THE RULE OF LAW. More important still, alongside the statutory changes there arose A SPECIAL LAW OF POLICE AND SECRET POLICE OPERATIONS, ALMOST ENTIRELY DETACHED FROM CONSTITUTIONAL RULES, including the special powers of the party and the SS, applied chiefly in the newly conquered territories in the east. JEWS WERE SOON WHOLLY EXCLUDED FROM ALL REMAINING NORMS that afforded even minimal protection in proceedings.

terms.def: Founding criminal liability where it is certain that the accused committed a crime but not which of several — contrary to the principle in dubio pro reo.

cards.q: What did the Nazis need criminal law for politically?
cards.a: To intimidate political opponents, suppress minorities, CREATE FEAR — NOT LEAST AMONG THEIR OWN FOLLOWERS — and to WELD THE VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT TOGETHER BY CRIMINALISING A FEW EXPOSED VICTIMS: the 'November criminals', communists and Jews. They had no programme of criminal law reform; they had only an anti-liberal, anti-rational and anti-individualist tone.

cards.q: Which three principles of criminal law did the regime break through?
cards.a: The PROHIBITION OF RETROACTIVITY (Rückwirkungsverbot), the PROHIBITION OF ANALOGY (Analogieverbot) and the principle IN DUBIO PRO REO — by introducing Wahlfeststellung, criminal liability where it was clear that the accused had committed a crime but not which of several. This undermined the very core of criminal justice under the rule of law.

19.title: Special courts and military justice
19.text: AS EARLY AS 1933 SPECIAL COURTS were established in the district of every higher regional court with the aim of punishing acts under the Reichstag Fire Decree and the MALICE ACT AS QUICKLY AND SEVERELY AS POSSIBLE; their procedure was drastically shortened and THERE WAS NO APPEAL. During the war their competences expanded substantially and the rights of defendants were further pared away — so that the special courts became, in the regime's own words, 'THE COURTS MARTIAL OF THE HOME FRONT'. 'According to the public necessities in the incorporated eastern territories' the police summary courts, SS COURTS and wholly lawless executive acts then PAID NO REGARD WHATEVER TO CONSTITUTIONAL STANDARDS. MILITARY JUSTICE went the same way: abolished in 1919 except for a state of war and for ships, it was now immediately restored. At first there were three instances with the Reich Court at the apex; after 1934 jurisdiction passed to the VOLKSGERICHTSHOF and two years later to the REICH COURT MARTIAL. The substantive basis was the MILITARY CRIMINAL CODE OF 1872, to which the Nazis added special wartime criminal law prepared in 1938 and promulgated in 1939, revising the whole code on 10 October 1940. And the result: AFTER 1941 MILITARY JUSTICE TURNED FROM A SPECIAL JURISDICTION ORIGINALLY ESTABLISHED ON CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLES INTO AN INSTRUMENT OF TERROR THAT KILLED SOME 30,000 PEOPLE.

cards.q: What were the special courts and what did the regime itself call them?
cards.a: Courts established as early as 1933 in the district of every higher regional court to punish, as quickly and severely as possible, acts under the Reichstag Fire Decree and the Malice Act; procedure was shortened and THERE WAS NO APPEAL. During the war they became, in the regime's own words, 'THE COURTS MARTIAL OF THE HOME FRONT'.

cards.q: What became of military justice?
cards.a: Abolished in 1919, it was immediately restored; jurisdiction passed after 1934 to the Volksgerichtshof and two years later to the Reich Court Martial. AFTER 1941 IT TURNED FROM A SPECIAL JURISDICTION ORIGINALLY ESTABLISHED ON CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLES INTO AN INSTRUMENT OF TERROR THAT KILLED SOME 30,000 PEOPLE.

20.title: The balance sheet of criminal law
20.text: KARL PETERS summed it up by saying that criminal law and criminal practice 'NOT ONLY ERECTED A PROTECTIVE BARRIER AROUND THE SYSTEM OF VIOLENCE BUT ALSO CREATED… A TERRIBLE BLOODBATH BY THE CONSISTENT ENFORCEMENT OF RACIAL IDEOLOGY AND THE RESULTING EXTERMINATION OF SUPPOSEDLY INFERIOR PEOPLE'. Nazism did put into practice a few points of the Weimar reform debate — protective measures, the DUAL TRACK OF LEGAL CONSEQUENCES (ZWEISPURIGKEIT), the differentiation of guilt in murder and manslaughter and among multiple participants, and the accessory character of aiding the principal offence — BUT THOSE STEPS WERE FAR OUTWEIGHED BY THE ABANDONMENT OF FRANZ VON LISZT'S REFORM LINE AND THE REMOVAL OF THE PROCEDURAL GUARANTEES DEVELOPED SINCE THE ENLIGHTENMENT. After 1933 practice and literature were dominated by: THE BREACH OF DUTIES TO THE VOLKSGEMEINSCHAFT INSTEAD OF THE BREACH OF RIGHTS; PUNISHING THE PERPETRATOR INSTEAD OF THE ACT; THE LOOSENING OF DEFINITIONS OF OFFENCES BY THE INTRODUCTION OF IDEOLOGICAL CONCEPTS; THE WIDENING OF SENTENCING RANGES; THE PRIORITY OF DETERRENCE OVER RESOCIALISATION; THE STRENGTHENING OF THE PROSECUTOR AND THE RESTRICTION OF DEFENCE RIGHTS; THE RESTRICTION OF APPEALS; THE INTRODUCTION OF SPECIAL COURTS, ABOVE ALL THE VOLKSGERICHTSHOF BY THE ACT OF 24 APRIL 1934; AND THE FORMAL ABOLITION OF THE PRINCIPLE OF LEGALITY BY DECREE OF 13 DECEMBER 1944.

cards.q: List the features that dominated criminal practice and literature after 1933.
cards.a: Breach of DUTIES to the Volksgemeinschaft instead of breach of RIGHTS; punishing the PERPETRATOR instead of the act; loosening of definitions of offences by ideological concepts; widening of sentencing ranges; priority of DETERRENCE over resocialisation; strengthening of the prosecutor and restriction of the defence; restriction of appeals; special courts including the Volksgerichtshof (24 April 1934); and the formal abolition of THE PRINCIPLE OF LEGALITY by decree of 13 December 1944.

21.title: The internationally oriented disciplines and the impossibility of a Nazi legal philosophy
21.text: The branches with an international dimension — private international law, comparative law, the sociology of law, international law — were particularly affected by the regime's racism. Their representatives could adopt VÖLKISCH views, but THE TRANSNATIONAL INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF THEIR FIELD MADE THOSE IDEAS DIFFICULT TO PUT INTO PRACTICE. The most important comparative lawyer, ERNST RABEL (1874–1955), who founded the discipline in its modern form, HAD TO GO INTO EXILE. The internationalists at first continued the previous line (loosening Versailles, the order of the League of Nations), and AFTER 1938 new approaches appeared which sought to interpret international law IN THE LIGHT OF THE REGIME'S RACISM and to think the international order in terms of 'GREAT EMPIRES' — the most important being CARL SCHMITT, Gustav Adolf Walz, Norbert Gürke, Reinhard Höhn and Werner Best, with a strong polemic against UNIVERSALISM, LIBERALISM AND PACIFISM in international law. And now the essential sentence: NATIONAL SOCIALISM COULD NOT HAVE A LEGAL PHILOSOPHY OF ITS OWN. Nazi 'ideology' was A MIXTURE OF INHUMAN OBSESSIONS AND FANTASIES OF VIOLENCE AND SUPERIORITY, FUSED WITH SOCIAL DARWINISM AND THE EUGENICS OF THE DAY. In the philosophy faculties a mixture arose of phenomenology, value theory and above all a NEO-IDEALISM building on Hegel (Julius Binder, KARL LARENZ, Ernst Rudolf Huber, Walter Schönfeld), but also on Leibniz, Fichte, Schelling, Nietzsche and contemporary existentialism. To this were added 'CONCRETE ORDER AND SHAPING THINKING' (KONKRETES ORDNUNGS- UND GESTALTUNGSDENKEN), approaches of a 'VÖLKISCH NATURAL LAW' and even a 'LEGAL DOCTRINE OF THE RACE LAWS'. What they all had in common was A CONSISTENTLY NEGATIVE STANCE TOWARDS EMPIRICISM, RATIONALISM, POSITIVISM AND SCIENTIFIC THEORY — which is why they remained AN EXCEPTIONAL EPISODE in the history of philosophy. And yet they contributed substantially to the regime, BECAUSE THEIR RHETORIC HELPED TO IDEALISE A BRUTAL REALITY.

cards.q: Why could Nazism not have a legal philosophy of its own?
cards.a: Because its 'ideology' was A MIXTURE OF INHUMAN OBSESSIONS AND FANTASIES OF VIOLENCE AND SUPERIORITY fused with social Darwinism and eugenics. What did arise — neo-idealism after Hegel, 'concrete order thinking', 'völkisch natural law' — shared A CONSISTENTLY NEGATIVE STANCE TOWARDS EMPIRICISM, RATIONALISM, POSITIVISM AND SCIENTIFIC THEORY and remained an exceptional episode. It contributed to the regime, though, in that ITS RHETORIC HELPED TO IDEALISE A BRUTAL REALITY.

cards.q: Why was it particularly hard for the internationally oriented disciplines to satisfy the regime?
cards.a: Because THE TRANSNATIONAL INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF THE FIELD made völkisch ideas difficult to put into practice — and key figures went into exile, for example ERNST RABEL, the founder of modern comparative law. After 1938 attempts nevertheless appeared to interpret international law racially and to think the order in terms of 'great empires' (Carl Schmitt and others).

22.title: Roman law and the Germanists
22.text: There was no independent Nazi historiography, and NO GENUINELY NAZI LEGAL HISTORY COULD ARISE EITHER. Most of the leading ROMANISTS EMIGRATED and Roman law was seriously threatened: POINT 19 OF THE NSDAP PROGRAMME read 'WE DEMAND THAT ROMAN LAW, WHICH SERVES A MATERIALIST WORLD ORDER, BE REPLACED BY A GERMAN COMMON LAW'. The discipline therefore renamed itself 'ANCIENT LEGAL HISTORY' but continued to struggle. In their defence the romanists pointed to FASCIST ITALY, WHERE THE REGIME EMPHASISED THE ROMAN TRADITION; they further argued that the reception of Roman law concerned METHODS RATHER THAN THE CONTENT of legal thought ('SCIENTIFICATION'), and that one must DISTINGUISH THE FLOURISHING AND THE DECLINE of Roman law. THE GERMANISTS by contrast felt themselves on the rise — their view of historical law had been shaped since the 19th century by national and Germanophile theses — and they now inclined towards the idealist and nationalist slogans of propaganda and SOUGHT THE GERMANIC 'ROOTS' OF GERMAN LAW. BUT apart from occasional cooperation with Himmler's 'AHNENERBE' and a few sycophantic rhetorical gestures TOWARDS THE IDEOLOGICAL CORE OF THE REGIME, THERE WAS NO REORIENTATION OF THE METHODOLOGY OR CONTENT OF THE DISCIPLINE.

cards.q: How did Roman law defend itself against point 19 of the NSDAP programme?
cards.a: Point 19 demanded the replacement of Roman law by a 'German common law'. The romanists renamed themselves 'ANCIENT LEGAL HISTORY' and defended themselves with three arguments: pointing to FASCIST ITALY, where the regime emphasised the Roman tradition; claiming that the reception concerned METHODS rather than content ('scientification'); and distinguishing the flourishing from the decline of Roman law. Most of the leading romanists had, however, emigrated.

23.title: Conclusion: a law that lost even its limited autonomy
23.text: Law as the body of norms that constitute a state and govern public life IS AUTONOMOUS FROM POLITICS AND THE ECONOMY ONLY TO A LIMITED AND FLUCTUATING DEGREE — AND AFTER 1933 IT DRAMATICALLY LOST EVEN THAT LIMITED AUTONOMY. The Nazi regime had, historically speaking, A FAIRLY SHORT LIFE. It committed one violation of law after another, BUT FOR TACTICAL REASONS IT RELUCTANTLY RESPECTED THE OVERALL NORMATIVE FRAMEWORK — AND PRECISELY FOR AS LONG AS IT REGARDED THE SUPPORT OF ADMINISTRATION AND ARMY AS NECESSARY. Because of the new level of aggression (1938/9), the growing power of the SS — which was becoming A STATE WITHIN THE STATE — and the outbreak of war, conventional law lost ITS CAPACITY FOR SELF-ASSERTION. ONLY THOSE WHO IGNORED THE BINDING FORCE OF LAW REACHED THE TOP OF THE POLITICAL LEADERSHIP. And that disintegration of law — which finally reached a state of complete 'ANOMIE' — would probably have led to the collapse of the regime EVEN WITHOUT THE WAR. The experience of the regime profoundly shaped the constitution, the legal order and the whole society of post-war Germany — and of course of the new STATE OF ISRAEL. The judicial reckoning with the Nazi past took MORE THAN SIX DECADES. And a final sentence: ALL OVER THE WORLD THE CRIMES AND VIOLATIONS OF LAW BY THE NAZI REGIME ARE REMEMBERED AS THE EMBODIMENT OF ATROCITY — AND THE REGIME HAS THEREBY ALSO BECOME A COMPARATIVE POINT OF REFERENCE THAT GIVES US THE MEANS TO CONDEMN NEW ROGUE STATES AND NEW FORMS OF GENOCIDE.

cards.q: How long and why did the regime respect the normative framework?
cards.a: Reluctantly and FOR TACTICAL REASONS — PRECISELY FOR AS LONG AS IT REGARDED THE SUPPORT OF ADMINISTRATION AND ARMY AS NECESSARY. Because of the new aggression of 1938/9, the growing power of the SS as a state within the state and the outbreak of war, conventional law lost its capacity for self-assertion, and only those who ignored the binding force of law reached the top.

cards.q: What twofold significance does the Nazi regime have today, on Stolleis's account?
cards.a: The experience of it profoundly shaped the constitution, the legal order and the whole society of post-war Germany and of the new state of Israel — and it has at the same time become A COMPARATIVE POINT OF REFERENCE THAT GIVES US THE MEANS TO CONDEMN NEW ROGUE STATES AND NEW FORMS OF GENOCIDE. The judicial reckoning with it took more than six decades.
